title: One-tap phone pairing: QR + auto-submit + reachable URLs
description:
The pairing flow shipped under lab-tracker-bbd works but has three manual steps that defeat the 'no friction' goal: the enrollment URL contains the laptop's origin (often 127.0.0.1, not phone-reachable), there's no QR code so the user has to ferry the URL manually, and the phone shows a label form before pairing.

This bead replaces all three with: server renders a phone-reachable enrollment URL (resolved from request.base_url, overridable via LAB_TRACKER_PUBLIC_BASE_URL); the enrollment response includes an inline-SVG QR code of that URL; the DevicesPage shows the QR prominently next to the copy-URL fallback; the EnrollPage auto-submits with a User-Agent-derived label as soon as it loads, so scanning the QR ends in 'paired and in capture' with one tap.
design: Use segno for QR rendering (pure-Python, SVG-native, no Pillow dep). Determine base URL preference order: explicit setting, then request.base_url, then a hostname warning. EnrollPage keeps a manual override path (?label=foo) so the user can pair multiple phones distinguishably if needed, but defaults to UA-derived label.
acceptance_criteria:
- /auth/devices/enrollment returns enrollment_url that points to the request's external host, not 127.0.0.1
- LAB_TRACKER_PUBLIC_BASE_URL setting overrides the derived host (for tunnels, prod)
- Response includes enrollment_qr_svg containing valid SVG QR encoding the enrollment URL
- DevicesPage renders the QR inline; copy-URL is the fallback
- EnrollPage auto-submits on load, no label form required, label sourced from User-Agent
- End-to-end smoke: scan QR on iPhone Camera, tap pop-up, lands at /app/capture as paired device with no further taps

title: Batch draft service: persist proposals + retry/dead-letter
description:
Service-level orchestration that ties together build_batch_graph_context (lab-tracker-jdy) and the pluggable draft_from_batch client (lab-tracker-641). Given a set of staged notes, it builds the context packet, calls the configured client, persists the resulting proposal set as a pending batch with full traceability back to the source notes, and handles model failures with bounded retries + a dead-letter record so the runner can surface them.

Splits out of lab-tracker-641 once the provider abstraction and the OpenAI client method landed; persistence touches the data model (GraphChangeSet currently ties to a single source note and needs either schema extension or a sibling BatchGraphDraft entity) and warrants its own commit and review pass.
design: Decide: extend GraphChangeSet to carry a list of source_note_ids, or introduce BatchGraphDraft wrapping multiple GraphChangeSets/change-set-equivalents. Either way, every operation in the persisted record must trace back to the note(s) that motivated it via existing source_refs. Retries: bounded (e.g. 3) with exponential backoff for transient HTTP errors; non-retryable validation failures go straight to dead-letter. Dead-letter is a persisted record with the failure category, error text, and the offending input so a human can inspect.
acceptance_criteria:
- create_batch_graph_draft(notes, *, user_hint=None, actor=None) on the service layer
- Persists a pending batch with operation-level traceability to source note ids
- Retries transient model errors with bounded attempts + backoff
- Dead-letter record on terminal failure with category, error, and input snapshot
- Tests cover: success path persistence, retry on transient error, dead-letter on terminal error, empty-batch short-circuit

title: Batch draft generator: configurable provider + OpenAI batch client

- Supports multi-note merge proposals
- Supports link proposals (note -> question/session/dataset)

- Failure modes (model timeout, invalid JSON) handled with retries + dead-letter

title: Batch context builder: assemble notes + graph slice for the model

Should include: the full set of unprocessed notes (text, transcripts, image references), the relevant slice of the graph (projects/questions/sessions touched by those notes, plus their immediate neighbors), and any prior batch decisions on related entities.

This is what differentiates the daily batch from per-note drafting ? the model can see multiple related notes together and propose merges/relationships it couldn't see one at a time.
acceptance_criteria:
- Given a set of staged notes, returns a context packet with: notes payload, relevant graph subgraph, recent related decisions
- Context size bounded (paginated or truncated with priority signals if oversized)
- Tested with synthetic batches of varying size and graph density

title: Daily batch runner: scheduled, idempotent draft job

- Job collects staged notes since last successful run watermark
- Idempotent: re-running same window does not create duplicate batches

title: Device-bound auth (passkey or long-lived device token) for phone
description:
Username + password on a phone keyboard is the single worst friction point. After the first desktop login, the user should pair their phone once (QR code from desktop, magic link, or WebAuthn passkey enrollment) and never type a password on the phone again.

Token lives in IndexedDB scoped to the installed PWA. Revocable from a 'My devices' page on desktop. No biometric requirement at this stage ? long-lived bearer token is acceptable for the trust model (single-user lab notebook).
design: Two options to evaluate: (a) WebAuthn passkey ? most secure, supported on modern iOS/Android, requires platform authenticator UX; (b) QR-code pair flow ? desktop generates a short-lived enrollment URL with embedded device-token signing material, phone scans, stores long-lived token. Option (b) is simpler to ship; option (a) is the long-term right answer. Pick one and document the reason.
acceptance_criteria:
- After first pairing, phone capture works without entering credentials
- Device tokens revocable from a desktop 'My devices' view
- Tokens scoped so they can call /notes/quick-capture and the share-target handler, nothing destructive
- Decision recorded for passkey vs. QR pair flow with rationale

All linking (question, session, dataset, analysis, claim) is deferred to the daily draft review (lab-tracker-cw3). The endpoint should return 202 Accepted with the staged note id; the client treats success as 'queued for daily review'.
acceptance_criteria:
- New route POST /notes/quick-capture accepts multipart asset + optional project_id
- Falls back to per-user device-default project when project_id omitted
- Returns 202 with note id; sets status='staged' for the daily batch to pick up
- Tests cover image, audio, and text-only variants

title: Add service worker for app shell cache and upload retry queue

This is what makes capture survive the network dropping in a microscope room or basement lab. Without it, a failed upload is a lost note.
acceptance_criteria:

- App loads fully offline after first visit
- Failed POST to /notes/quick-capture is queued in IndexedDB with full payload
- Queued uploads retry on 'online' event and on next app open

title: Epic: Daily AI graph-draft batch
description:
Replace per-note draft generation with a once-a-day batch. Drafting on every upload thrashes context and wastes model calls on incomplete information; a daily cadence lets the model see accumulated notes together, dedupe, propose coherent multi-note merges, and produce a single review queue.

Goal: each day, a scheduled job collects all notes that landed since the last run, builds a graph-aware context packet covering them, asks Claude to propose graph operations (new nodes, edges, claim updates), and stores the result as a pending batch in the existing graph-draft review UI. The human reviews once per day instead of per note.

Pairs with the 'PWA capture-first phone workflow' epic: capture cheaply through the day, review proposals in one sitting.
design: Batch is the unit of review, not the individual note. Runner is idempotent (re-runnable on the same window without duplicates). Context builder pulls unprocessed notes + the relevant graph slice (projects/questions touched). Draft generator can propose merges across multiple notes (e.g. three photos from the same gel become one observation). Review UI extends the existing graph-draft card pattern to a batch container.
acceptance_criteria:
- Scheduled runner executes daily, idempotently, with configurable window
- Batch context builder collects all notes since last successful run + relevant graph slice
- Claude draft generator produces a structured proposal set covering the batch
- Pending batches appear in the review UI with per-operation accept/reject
- Approved operations commit through the existing graph mutation path
- Rejected/edited operations are recorded for future model feedback
- Notification surfaces when a new batch is ready for review

title: Epic: PWA capture-first phone workflow
description:
Make phone note capture nearly effortless. The current /app/capture screen requires login, mandatory project selection, and a network round-trip before anything is saved ? too much friction for one-handed bench work.

Goal: a user takes a photo with their phone's normal Camera app, hits Share, picks Lab Tracker, and the note is staged. No browser open, no login each time, no fields required beyond the captured asset.

This requires turning the existing static-bundle frontend into a Progressive Web App: web app manifest (Add to Home Screen), service worker (offline asset cache + upload retry queue), Web Share Target (OS share-sheet integration), and a device-bound auth path (passkey or long-lived device token) that eliminates the password prompt on phone. The note API also needs a minimal-payload quick-capture endpoint that accepts asset + device-default project and defers all linking to the daily draft review.

Pairs with the 'Daily AI graph-draft batch' epic: capture cheaply now, AI proposes structured graph updates once a day for human review.
design: Phone capture flow target: Camera -> Share Sheet -> Lab Tracker -> staged. <3 taps, works offline. Auth via device-bound passkey/token in IndexedDB, not username/password. Quick-capture endpoint accepts only asset + project; everything else (question/session/dataset links) gets proposed by the daily batch and confirmed in the review card.
acceptance_criteria:
- manifest.json served with icons, theme, start URL
- Service worker caches the app shell and queues failed uploads with retry
- Web Share Target registered so OS share sheet routes photos to a capture endpoint
- POST /notes/quick-capture accepts minimal payload (asset + project_id), returns 202 if queued
- Device-bound auth path lets a phone authenticate without typing a password on each visit
- Offline capture survives a network drop and syncs when connectivity returns
- iOS and Android smoke-tested via lab-tracker-e45

title: Clarify and harden MCP note creation validation for status and metadata
description:
While recording the 2026-04-28 temporal-gradient projector titration analysis through the Lab Tracker MCP connector, `lab_tracker_create_note` accepted only a reduced payload after two confusing validation failures.

Observed behavior:
- Creating a note with `status="active"` failed, while the analogous question flow accepts `active`. This is technically consistent with `NoteStatus` (`staged`, `committed`, `archived`), but the MCP tool exposes `status` as a free string and the skill/API docs do not make the note-specific allowed values obvious.
- Creating a note with structured metadata failed unless all metadata values were strings. `NoteCreate.metadata` is typed as `dict[str, str]`, so Pydantic rejects non-string JSON values before the request reaches `_normalize_note_metadata`, even though the service normalizer is written to coerce non-string values to strings.
- The successful fallback was to create the note with `status="staged"` and no metadata, which avoided data loss but made the assistant workflow more brittle and less informative.

Concrete example context:
- Project: `b97935f1-42c6-475d-b35f-0e23607d11e6`
- Successful fallback note: `4dc2ec50-7781-475d-ba3d-b89c0c79895b`
- MCP tool: `lab_tracker_create_note`
- Relevant code paths noticed during triage: `src/lab_tracker/schemas.py` (`NoteCreate.metadata: dict[str, str]`, `status: NoteStatus | None`), `src/lab_tracker/mcp_server.py` (`lab_tracker_create_note(status: str | None, metadata: dict[str, str] | None)`), and `src/lab_tracker/services/shared.py` (`_normalize_note_metadata` coerces values).

Why this matters:
Assistant clients will naturally use project/question status vocabulary and structured provenance metadata. The current behavior requires hidden knowledge of note-specific status values and silently discourages preserving useful machine-readable provenance on notes.
acceptance_criteria:
- `lab_tracker_create_note` docs/schema expose the allowed note statuses (`staged`, `committed`, `archived`) clearly, or the MCP layer rejects invalid statuses with a targeted error before the generic API failure.
- Decide whether note metadata should accept JSON scalar values and normalize them, or remain string-only; make the API schema, service normalizer, MCP type hints, and docs agree.
- Add or update tests for MCP note creation covering invalid note status and metadata values with at least one non-string scalar.
- Update the Lab Tracker skill/docs so assistant clients know the note status vocabulary and metadata contract.
close_reason: Clarified note status validation and aligned scalar metadata handling across API, MCP, tests, docs, and installed skills.
